messages.content: You design amateur rockets that fly on certified commercial motors. Work through the design, check it with the tools, and give the final design as JSON inside <design> tags. Only report results the tools returned.
Design a rocket that goes about 175 m. The field is low-power only, so D or smaller. Keep it under 1 in diameter. Expect about 4 m/s of wind.

messages.reasoning_content:
1. Understand: apogee is about 175 m, so the band is 175 * 0.95 = 166 m to 175 * 1.05 = 184 m. Motor class is D or smaller. Diameter is under 1 inch, and 1 * 0.0254 = 0.0254 m, so the body has to be narrower than that. Wind is about 4 m/s and goes in every flight call. Landing speed is not stated, so I assume 6 m/s. Rail is not stated, so 1.5 m. Single stage, vertical, sea level.
2. Feasibility: 175 m with no drag is sqrt(2 * 9.81 * 175) = 59 m/s. A C or a D on a tube this skinny will overshoot. A B is the right class. Looking up B6 and C6.

2. Feasibility: C6 is 8.8 N*s and B6 is 4.3 N*s, so 8.8 / 4.3 = 2.0 times the impulse. On a tube under an inch that extra impulse would sail past 175 m. B6 is 5.2 N average, 12.1 N peak, 18 mm, 0.016 kg, and its only delay is 0 s. I'll plug it and open one chute at apogee. The body outer diameter will be 0.0248 m, under 0.0254 m.
3. Size: guessed mass 0.050 kg with a little nose mass, because a bare B6 rocket on this diameter coasts high. Descent mass is about 0.050 - 0.006 = 0.044 kg. A 5 m/s landing, under the assumed 6 m/s, needs 2 * 0.044 * 9.81 / (1.225 * 0.8 * 5^2) = 0.035 m^2, diameter sqrt(4 * 0.035 / 3.1416) = 0.21 m. I'll fit a 0.24 m chute.
4. Draft: 24.8 mm cardboard body, 0.38 m long, 0.008 kg in the nose, three modest balsa fins so a 4 m/s wind does not weathercock it hard. Wind in the call is 4 m/s.

4. Check: the simulator gives apogee 190.2 m. The band top is 175 * 1.05 = 184 m, and 190.2 - 184 = 6 m over it. Landing is 4.2 m/s, under 6. Rail exit is 26.7 m/s, thrust-to-weight is 11.8, and margin is 3.16 cal. The body is 24.8 mm, under 1 inch, and the motor is a B6. Wind in the run was 4 m/s. The only miss is altitude.
5. Fix: raise the nose mass from 0.008 kg to 0.012 kg. Six metres is a small miss, so a small mass change. Chute, fins, motor, and the 4 m/s wind stay.

4. Check: the simulator gives apogee 180.8 m. That is 180.8 - 175 = 5.8 m over the target, and the 5% band is 0.05 * 175 = 8.8 m, so it is inside. Landing is 4.4 m/s, under 6. Rail exit is 25.1 m/s, thrust-to-weight is 10.8, and margin is 3.64 cal. Body diameter is 0.0248 m, and 0.0254 - 0.0248 = 0.0006 m under 1 inch. The motor is a B6, inside the D cap. Wind in the run was 4 m/s. The chute opened. Every check passes.
5. Fix: no further change; the altitude band, the diameter, and the safety gates all pass.
6. Uncertainty: 5.8 m over 175 m is inside the band, and a heavier build than the 0.049 kg liftoff mass will fall out the bottom. Margin is 3.64 cal in a 4 m/s wind, so it will weathercock some; drift in the run was 149 m. Chute Cd is a model 0.8. The B6 catalog entry has no delay grain, so the apogee chute is the recovery.
messages.content:
Estes B6 in a 24.8 mm cardboard rocket, 0.45 m long, under 1 inch, with 0.012 kg in the nose and a 0.24 m chute at apogee.
In 4 m/s wind the apogee is 180.8 m, inside the band around 175 m, and the landing is 4.4 m/s.
Rail exit is 25.1 m/s at 3.64 cal.
